DAMGHANI:v1p320/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p320/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p320/r9.claim: Yaʿrishūn means the structures people build.
DAMGHANI:v1p320/r9.anchor: العرش البنيان قوله تعالى في سورة النحل واوحى ربك الى النحل

QUSHAYRI:v2p162/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p162/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p162/r2.claim: God’s revelation to the bee means inspiration; because it obeys and eats lawfully, its honey is wholesome and healing.
QUSHAYRI:v2p162/r2.anchor: أوحى إلى النحل : أراد به وحي إلهام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p558/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p558/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p558/r9.claim: Revelation to the bee means inspiration and instruction placed in its heart, whose true nature humans cannot know.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p558/r9.anchor: والإيحاء هنا الإلهام والإلقاء في روعها، وتعليمها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r2.claim: النحل is a collective whose singular is نحلة; it is feminine in the Hijaz dialect, hence the feminine imperative اتخذي; Ibn Waththāb reads fatḥa on ḥāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r2.anchor: نحلة، ويؤنث في لغة الحجاز، ولذلك قال: أن اتخذي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī takes أن as explanatory because revelation includes speech; the author objects that the commentators agree it means inspiration, which has no speech element.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله الرازي: أن هي المفسرة لما في الوحي من معنى القول، هذا قول جمهور المفسرين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī marvels that innate inspiration enables bees to build precise hexagonal cells, obey a larger leader, and return to their hive when summoned by drums and music.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r4.anchor: منها بناؤها البيوت المسدسة من أضلاع، متساوية بمجرد طباعها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r5.claim: The first من is partitive: bees do not build in every mountain, tree, trellis, or place. The shelters include mountain crevices and hollow trees, while human trellises refer to hives and wall cavities.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r5.anchor: ومن للتبعيض لأنها لا تبني في كل جبل، وكل شجر، وكل ما يعرش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues the bees' houses are the structures they build, since the verse's partitive wording means they do not build in every mountain, tree, or trellis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ما يدل على أن البيوت ليست الكوى، وإنما هي ما تبنيه هي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the trellises as grapevines; al-Ṭabarī says roofs people construct, while Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls both explanations imprecise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r7.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: ومما يعرشون الكروم. وقال الطبري: مما يبنون من السقوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r8.claim: Bees occur both wild in mountains and woodland and managed in people's hives, so the command encompasses both kinds; the reading of يعرشون differs in the vowel on rāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r8.anchor: ولما كان النحل نوعين: منه ما مقره في الجبال والغياض ولا يتعهده أحد

FARRA:v2p109/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p109/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p109/r3.claim: God's inspiration to the bees means He instilled guidance in them; no messenger was sent to them.
FARRA:v2p109/r3.anchor: وأوحى ربك إلى النحل [68] ألهمها ولم يأتها رسول

FARRA:v2p109/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p109/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p109/r4.claim: يعرشون refers to the structures or roofs people build.
FARRA:v2p109/r4.anchor: ومن الشجر ومما يعرشون) وهي سقوف البيوت

MAJAZ:v1p363/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p363/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p363/r5.claim: Yaʿrush and yaʿrish are both used for making a trellis or arbor.
MAJAZ:v1p363/r5.anchor: «ومما يعرشون» (68) أي يجعلونه عريشا، ويقال: يعرش ويعرش

NAHHAS:v2p402/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p402/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p402/r2.claim: The bee is feminine; its diminutive is naḥīl without tāʾ so it will not resemble the singular form.
NAHHAS:v2p402/r2.anchor: لأنها مؤنثة والعرب تقول في تصغيرها : نحيل بغير هاء لئلا تشبه الواحدة

NAHHAS:v2p402/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p402/r3.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v2p402/r3.claim: He also reports that Arabs use the bee noun as masculine.

NAHHAS:v2p402/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p402/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p402/r4.claim: The plural ‘houses’ follows the pattern of fulūs; reading its bāʾ with kasra substitutes kasra for the damma, a remote analysis.
NAHHAS:v2p402/r4.anchor: بيوتا ) ^ كما تقول ؛ فلس وفلوس ومن كسر الباء أبدل من الضمة كسرة وهو وجه بعيد

DURR-FULL:v5p142#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p142#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p142#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses God's revelation to the bee as inspiration; Hasan says it is cast into its heart, and Mujahid says no messenger was sent to it.
DURR-FULL:v5p142#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وأوحى ربك إلى النحل} قال: ألهمها

DURR-FULL:v5p142#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p142#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p142#2/r9.claim: Hasan says the bee is smaller than a locust and that its revelation is an inspiration cast into its heart.
DURR-FULL:v5p142#2/r9.anchor: عن الحسن قال: النحل دابة أصغر من الجندب ووحيه إليها قذف في قلوبها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r1.claim: Waḥy in Arabic is a hidden conveyance of meaning; here it is inspiration rather than prophetic revelation, as interpreters agree, though the word can also mean command.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r1.anchor: كما قال تعالى بأن ربك أوحى لها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r2.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab reads إلى النخل with a fatḥa on the ḥāʾ; أن introduces an explanation of the inspiration.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r2.anchor: بفتح الحاء وأن في قوله أن اتخذي مفسرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r3.claim: God made bee homes in mountain crevices, hollow trees, and human-made structures such as hives and walls.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r3.anchor: إما في الجبال وكواها، وإما في متجوف الأشجار، وإما فيما يعرش ابن آدم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r4.claim: ʿArsh means to prepare or arrange, especially branches and wood into a crafted, shaded structure; the term is used for the shelter made for the Prophet at Badr.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r4.anchor: معناه هيأ، وأكثر ما يستعمل فيما يكون من إتقان الأغصان والخشب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r5.claim: The verb yaʿrishūn is read with either kasra or ḍamma; Ibn Zayd says it means vines, while al-Tabari says roofs, and the author finds both explanations imprecise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r5.anchor: وقال ابن زيد في قوله: يعرشون قال الكروم، وقال الطبري ومما يعرشون يعني ما يبنون من السقوف

JISHUMI:v6p4066#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4066#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4066#2/r4.claim: Dhullul is the plural of dhalūl, something made easy to travel; it can describe a trodden path and is opposed to difficulty.
JISHUMI:v6p4066#2/r4.anchor: والذلل: جمع ذلول، يقال: دابة ذلول بين الذل، ورجل ذليل بين الذل بضم الذال،

MUQATIL:16:68-70/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:68-70/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:68-70/r1.claim: God's revelation to the bee is inspiration cast into it; it makes homes in mountains, trees, and human-built structures.
MUQATIL:16:68-70/r1.anchor: قال: { وأوحى ربك إلى النحل } إلهاما من الله عز وجل، يقول: قذف فيها،

ZAJJAJ:v3p209/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p209/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p209/r3.claim: بيوت with ḍamma follows the regular pattern; kasra is explained by the following yāʾ, though Basran grammarians reject that pattern.
ZAJJAJ:v3p209/r3.anchor: فمن قرأ بيوتا بالضم فهو القياس، مثل كعب وكعوب وقلب

ZAJJAJ:v3p209/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p209/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p209/r4.claim: Wahy includes communication and understanding, prophetic revelation and inspiration; God inspires creatures to seek benefit and avoid harm.
ZAJJAJ:v3p209/r4.anchor: ومعنى الوحي في اللغة على وجهين يرجعان إلى معنى الإعلام والإفهام

ASAD-NOTES:16:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:intro/r2.claim: The title points to the bee as an instance of divine creativity, while evidence of God's purposeful activity culminates in the ethical injunctions of verse 90.
ASAD-NOTES:16:intro/r2.anchor: the evidence of the Creator's purposeful activity that provides the subject-matter of most of this surah

STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r7.claim: The surah takes its name from its account of God's revelation to the bee.
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r7.anchor: The sūrah takes its name from the discussion of God’s revelation to the bee in vv. 68–69.

TABATABAI:16:67-69/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r3.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib defines revelation as rapid indication, conveyed by coded speech, unstructured sound, gesture, or another hidden means that delivers meaning to its intended recipient.
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r3.anchor: الإشارة السريعة وذلك يكون بالكلام على سبيل الرمز

TABATABAI:16:67-69/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r4.claim: Qurʾānic wahy includes instinctive inspiration to animals, inspiration in a dream, satanic whispering, signs or gestures, and divine communication to prophets.
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r4.anchor: فالإلهام بإلقاء المعنى في فهم الحيوان من طريق الغريزة من الوحي

TABATABAI:16:67-69/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r5.claim: Islamic religious etiquette reserves the unqualified term revelation for God’s communication with prophets and messengers.
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r5.anchor: وقد قرر الأدب الديني في الإسلام أن لا يطلق الوحي على غير ما عند الأنبياء والرسل

TABATABAI:16:67-69/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r6.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r6.claim: Al-Majmaʿ explains dhulul as the plural of dhalul, meaning docile or submissive, for an animal or a person.
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r6.anchor: والذلل جمع الذلول، يقال دابة ذلول بين الذل

TABATABAI:16:67-69/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r7.claim: God inspired the honeybee through instinct implanted in its constitution; its remarkable social life and craft may explain why the address shifts to the Prophet as your Lord revealed.
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r7.anchor: أي ألهمه من طريق غريزته التي أودعها في بنيته

TABATABAI:16:67-69/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r8.claim: The bee’s houses in what people trellis are probably structures people build for honey; eating from all fruits includes feeding on material in flowers before the fruit ripens.
TABATABAI:16:67-69/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بما يعرشون هو ما يبنون لبيوت العسل

TABRISI:16:67-69/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:67-69/r2.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:16:67-69/r2.claim: God’s revelation to the bee means inspiration, either according to al-Ḥasan, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Mujāhid or as an instinct planted in it that other creatures do not perceive, also attributed to al-Ḥasan.
TABRISI:16:67-69/r2.anchor: أي ألهمها إلهاما عن الحسن وابن عباس ومجاهد

TABRISI:16:67-69/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:67-69/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:16:67-69/r3.claim: God’s revelation to the bee means inspiration, either according to al-Ḥasan, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Mujāhid or as an instinct planted in it that other creatures do not perceive, also attributed to al-Ḥasan.
TABRISI:16:67-69/r3.anchor: أي ألهمها إلهاما عن الحسن وابن عباس ومجاهد

TABRISI:16:67-69/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:67-69/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:16:67-69/r4.claim: God’s revelation to the bee means inspiration, either according to al-Ḥasan, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Mujāhid or as an instinct planted in it that other creatures do not perceive, also attributed to al-Ḥasan.
TABRISI:16:67-69/r4.anchor: أي ألهمها إلهاما عن الحسن وابن عباس ومجاهد

TABRISI:16:67-69/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:67-69/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:16:67-69/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda lists Arabic senses of waḥy: prophetic revelation, inspiration, gesture, writing, and secret communication; he illustrates them with the cited Qur’anic passages.
TABRISI:16:67-69/r5.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة الوحي في كلام العرب على وجوه منها وحي النبوة ومنها الإلهام ومنها الإشارة

TABRISI:16:67-69/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:67-69/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:16:67-69/r6.claim: Mujāhid explains ‘he signaled to them’ as a gesture; al-Ḍaḥḥāk says it means he wrote for them.
TABRISI:16:67-69/r6.anchor: في قوله فأوحى إليهم أن سبحوا قال مجاهد معناه أشار إليهم وقال الضحاك كتب لهم

TABRISI:16:67-69/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:67-69/r7.speaker: الضحاك
TABRISI:16:67-69/r7.claim: Mujāhid explains ‘he signaled to them’ as a gesture; al-Ḍaḥḥāk says it means he wrote for them.
TABRISI:16:67-69/r7.anchor: قال مجاهد معناه أشار إليهم وقال الضحاك كتب لهم

TABRISI:16:67-69/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:67-69/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:16:67-69/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās’s statement that there is no revelation except the Qur’an refers to the Qur’an as the revelation brought by Gabriel to Muḥammad, not to every Arabic sense of waḥy.
TABRISI:16:67-69/r8.anchor: وأما ما روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال لا وحي إلا القرآن فإن المراد به أن القرآن هو الوحي الذي نزل به جبرائيل

TABRISI:16:67-69/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:67-69/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:67-69/r9.claim: In Arabic, waḥy is discreet, concealed communication; both awḥā lahu and awḥā ilayhi are used.
TABRISI:16:67-69/r9.anchor: وأصل الوحي عند العرب أن يلقي الإنسان إلى صاحبه شيئا بالاستتار والإخفاء

TABRISI:16:67-69/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:67-69/r10.speaker: العجاج
TABRISI:16:67-69/r10.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj’s line about the ground being told to settle illustrates waḥy as concealed communication or inspiration.
TABRISI:16:67-69/r10.anchor:
قال العجاج:
أوحى لها القرار فاستقرت

TABRISI:16:67-69/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:67-69/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:67-69/r11.claim: God inspired the bee to make homes for honey in mountains, trees, and other places, a capacity no person could devise without divine instruction.
TABRISI:16:67-69/r11.anchor: والمعنى أن الله تعالى ألهم النحل اتخاذ المنازل والمساكن والأوكار والبيوت في الجبال والشجر

TABRISI:16:67-69/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:67-69/r12.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:16:67-69/r12.claim: ‘From what people build’ can refer to grape arbors or to the beehives people construct; yaʿrishūn has two vowel patterns and can mean they build, from ʿarsh as a roof.
TABRISI:16:67-69/r12.anchor: والعرش سقف البيت عن الكلبي والمعنى ما يبني الناس لها

TABRISI:16:67-69/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:67-69/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:67-69/r13.claim: The bee receives commands in the wording because the verse first describes what is inspired to it, a rhetorical extension despite its inability to understand speech.
TABRISI:16:67-69/r13.anchor: وإنما أتى بلفظ الأمر وإن كانت النحل لا تعقل الأمر ولا تكون مأمورة لأنه لما أتى بلفظ الوحي

THALABI:v6p27/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p27/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p27/r9.claim: God's inspiration to bees means placing the knowledge in their hearing or instincts; النحل are honey-producing wasps, with نحلة as the singular.
THALABI:v6p27/r9.anchor: وأوحى ربك إلى النحل أي ألقى [على مسامعها] أو قذف في أنفسها ففهمته

THALABI:v6p27/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p27/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v6p27/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd says what people build trellises for means grapevines.
THALABI:v6p27/r10.anchor: ومن الشجر ومما يعرشون يبنون، وقال ابن زيد: هو الكرم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:66-68/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:66-68/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:66-68/r4.claim: God inspired and instilled in bees the means to make homes in mountains and trees.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:66-68/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:66-68/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:66-68/r5.claim: Wild bees make their own homes, whereas owned bees use the hives their keepers build for them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:66-68/r5.anchor: هي تتخذ لأنفسها بيوتا إذا كانت لا أصحاب لها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r2.claim: God inspired the bees, and their houses include places in mountains, trees, and structures people build.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r2.anchor: قوله: {وأوحى ربك إلى النحل} [النحل: 68] ، أي: ألهمها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r3.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says every kind of animal receives inspiration.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r3.anchor: قال السدي: وكل شيء من الحيوان إلهام.

ASAD-NOTES:16:68#n77/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:68#n77/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:68#n77/r1.claim: Awha highlights bee instinct: it builds an exceptionally ordered, economical honeycomb from proportioned hexagonal prismatic wax cells.
ASAD-NOTES:16:68#n77/r1.anchor: the wonderful quality of the instinct which enables the lowly insect to construct the geometrical masterpiece of a honeycomb out of perfectly-proportioned hexagonal, prismatic wax cells

ELMALILI:16:68-69/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:16:68-69/r1.speaker: müfessirîn
ELMALILI:16:68-69/r1.claim: Commentators understand the bee's revelation as inspiration, since it is plainly not prophetic revelation; the author accepts this distinction.
ELMALILI:16:68-69/r1.anchor: Buradaki “vahy”i müfessirîn vahy-i ilham diye tefsir etmişlerdir.

ELMALILI:16:68-69/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:16:68-69/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:16:68-69/r2.claim: Ilham means casting a meaning into the heart, but it does not entail obligatory or necessary knowledge or action.
ELMALILI:16:68-69/r2.anchor: “İlham” bir mânayı kalbe ilkādır. Fakat ilham, ilmî veya amelî bir vücub ve ıztırar ifade etmez.

ELMALILI:16:68-69/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:16:68-69/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:16:68-69/r3.claim: The bee's craft expresses necessary practical instinct; though not prophetic revelation, it resembles revelation in its necessary certainty and illustrates the force and accuracy of this spiritual phenomenon.
ELMALILI:16:68-69/r3.anchor: arının sanatı bir nübüvvet vahyi olmamakla beraber zarûrî bir hüküm ifade etmesi haysiyetiyle ona şebîhtir.

ELMALILI:16:68-69/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:16:68-69/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:16:68-69/r4.claim: God gives the bee an unfailing nature and craft for making honey; prophetic revelation likewise is necessary, divinely given knowledge, as indicated by ‘your Lord.’
ELMALILI:16:68-69/r4.anchor: Hak teâlâ tarafından arıya bal yapmak rûh ve sanatı şaşmaz bir vücub ve isabetle verildiği gibi, peygambere gelen vahiy de zarûrî bir ilm-i ledünnîdir.

ELMALILI:16:68-69/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:16:68-69/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:16:68-69/r5.claim: Revelation to the bee means God gives it this spirit and innate nature, secretly trains it without an outward intermediary, and teaches its sense and craft with perfect certainty.
ELMALILI:16:68-69/r5.anchor: gizli bir surette terbiye ederek ona o his ve sanatı kemâl-i kat‘iyyetle tâlim edip belletmek demektir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r1.claim: Here waḥy, rendered “inspired,” means God creates in creatures the skills needed to seek benefit, avoid harm, and sustain themselves; psychology calls this instinct, and Ibn al-Arabi is cited for the gloss.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r1.anchor: becerileri Allah Teâlâ’nın onda yaratması” anlamındaki ilham karşılığında kullanılmıştır (Ebû Bekir İbnü’l-Arabî, III, 1156).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r2.claim: The bees’ “houses” are combs with hexagonal cells, made from their own products in suitable natural places such as tree hollows or in hives prepared by people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r2.anchor: Arıya yapması ilham edilen “yuvalar”dan maksat, arıların ağaç kovukları gibi uygun doğal mekânlarda veya insanların özel olarak hazırladığı kovanlarda kendi ürünleriyle oluşturdukları petekler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r3.claim: By instinct, honeybees make their own nests from beeswax and arrange precisely measured hexagonal-prism cells within the comb.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r3.anchor: bizzat kendisinin ürettiği bal mumuyla kendi yuvasını yapmakta, dalak içine milimetrik ölçülerle altıgen prizma şeklinde gözcükler yerleştirmektedir.

BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r1.claim: God’s revelation to the bee means inspiration placed in its heart and instruction in a hidden manner; revelation can mean any subtle prompting.
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r1.anchor: ألهمها وقذف في قلوبها وعلمها بوجه لا يعلمه إلا هو

BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r2.claim: God inspires every animal to seek what benefits it and avoid what harms it.
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r2.anchor: والله تعالى ألهم كل حيوان أن يلتمس منافعه ويجنتب مضاره

BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r3.claim: God inspired a raven to dig in the earth, showing Cain how to conceal Abel’s body; Bursevī cites the Mathnawī on this lesson.
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r3.anchor: أن يبحث في الأرض ليرى قابيل كيف يواري سوءة أخيه هابيل

BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r4.speaker: الزجاج
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives the word النحل from God’s gifting honey to people, since النحلة means a gift.
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج : سميت نحلا لأن الله تعالى نحل الناس العسل الذي يخرج منها

BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r5.claim: The honeybee’s distinction is expressed in the saying that every fly is in the Fire except the honeybee.
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r5.anchor: وكل ذباب في النار إلا ذباب العسل

BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r6.speaker: عجائب المخلوقات
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r6.claim: A report calls Eid al-Fiṭr the Day of Mercy and says that on it the bee was inspired in the craft of making honey.
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r6.anchor: قال في عجائب المخلوقات : يقال ليوم عيد الفطر يوم الرحمة

BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r7.speaker: حياة الحيوان
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r7.claim: Eating bees is forbidden although honey is lawful, as human milk is lawful while human flesh is forbidden; killing bees is disliked.
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r7.anchor: قال في "حياة الحيوان" : يحرم أكل النحل وإن كان العسل حلالا

BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r8.speaker: التتمة
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r8.claim: Al-Tatimma validates selling bees in a hive when all are visible; if sold exposed, it validates that sale, whereas al-Tahdhīb gives the opposite ruling.

BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r9.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa disallows selling bees, like wasps and other insects, but allows selling silkworms used to produce silk.
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r9.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة : لا يصح بيع النحل كالزنبور وسائر الحشرات ويجوز بيع دود القز

BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r10.claim: The feminine imperative اتخذي is used because النحل may be grammatically masculine or feminine; the command means to take homes for itself.
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r10.anchor: لنفسك أي : بأن اتخذي فإن مصدرية وصيغة التأنيث لأن النحل يذكر ويؤنث

BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r11.claim: Bee cells are hexagonal and precisely fitted without instruments, a craft beyond even skilled engineers; hexagons leave no gaps and are roomier than other polygons.
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r11.anchor: لما في بيوته المسدسة المتساوية بلا بركار ومسطر من الحذاقة وحسن الصنعة

BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r12.claim: The partitive مِن indicates bees do not build in every mountain or every tree.
BURSEVI:v5p38#3/r12.anchor: ومن للتبعيض لأنها لا تبنى في كل جبل

BURSEVI:v5p39/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p39/r1.claim: The reference to places people trellis applies to selected human-built nesting places associated with property owners; bees do not use every such structure.
BURSEVI:v5p39/r1.anchor: لأنها لا تبنى في كل ما يعرشه الناس

BURSEVI:v5p39/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v5p39/r2.claim: Some explain human trellises as vines, roofs, walls, and other structures.
BURSEVI:v5p39/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم ومما يعرشون من كرم أو سقف أو جدران أو غير ذلك

QIRAAT-ER:16:68:10#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:16:68:10#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:16:68:10#1/r1.claim: Kasra on bāʾ yields biyūt rather than buyūt, a dialectal plural vowel with no semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:16:68:10#1/r1.anchor: dialectal voweling of the broken plural, no semantic change

QIRAAT-ER:16:68:16#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:16:68:16#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:16:68:16#1/r1.claim: The rāʾ may take ḍamma rather than kasra; both Form I patterns have the same meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:16:68:16#1/r1.anchor: both are valid Form I patterns, no semantic change

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p357#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p357#5/r1.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p357#5/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says God’s inspiration to the bees means He cast it into their nature.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p357#5/r1.anchor: عن الكلبي في قوله تعالى ﴿ وأوحى ربك إلى النحل ﴾ قال قذف في أنفسها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r1.claim: God's revelation to bees means inspiration, casting guidance into their hearts and teaching them in a way known only to the All-Knowing; some instead understand it as subjugation.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r1.anchor: ألهمها وألقى في روعها وعلمها بوجه لا يعلمه إلا اللطيف الخبير وفسر بعضهم الإحياء إليها بتسخيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r2.claim: Some deny that revelation is literal because it is reserved for rational beings, though bee behavior can make them seem intelligent and remarkably skilled.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r2.anchor: ومنعوا أن يكون المراد حقيقة الإحياء لأنه إنما يكون للعقلاء وليس التحل منها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r3.claim: Bees have a large leader, called the yaʿsub or emir, whose judgments the others follow and whom the colony serves.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r3.anchor: فتراها يكون بينها واحد كالرئيس هو أعظمها جثة يكون ناقد الحكم على سائرها والكل يخدمونه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r4.claim: When frightened, bees move collectively; people can reportedly call them home with drums and musical instruments, whose melodies lead them back.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r4.anchor: أنها إذا نفرت عن وكرها ذهبت بجمعيتها إلى موضع آخر فإذا أرادوا عودها إلى وكرها ضربوا لها الطبول

ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r5.claim: Bees construct equal-sided cells with precision beyond what people can manage without tools, and choose hexagonal cells because other shapes leave wasted gaps; these wonders display divine guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r5.anchor: وهي تبني البيوت من أضلاع متساوية والعقلاء لا يمكنهم ذلك إلا بآلات مثل المسطرة والفرجار

ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r6.speaker: الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r6.claim: Sufis, as al-Shaʿrani reports, permit literal revelation to bees and claim that animals have messengers and prophets; the author says revealed law rejects this.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r6.anchor: والصوفية على ما ذكره الشعراني في غير موضع لا يمنعون إرادة الحقيقة وقد أثبتوا في سائر الحيوانات رسلا وأنبياء

ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r7.speaker: بعض حكماء الإشراق
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r7.claim: Some Illuminationist philosophers say all animals possess rational souls; the author nearly concedes the claim but says he has heard the stronger animal-prophet claim only from Sufis.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r7.anchor: وذهب بعض حكماء الإشراق إلى ثبوت النفس الناطقة لجميع الحيوانات وأكاد أسلم لهم ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r8.claim: Al-nahl is a collective noun whose singular is nakhlah; Hijazi Arabic treats it as feminine, explaining the feminine imperative take.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r8.anchor: والنحل جنس واحده نحلة ويؤنث في لغة الحجاز ولذلك قال سبحانه : ( أن اتخذي

ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r9.speaker: ابن وثاب
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r9.claim: Ibn Waththab reads al-nahl with two fathas; the form may be dialectal or vowel harmony with the preceding nun.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب ( النحل ) بفتحتين وهو يحتمل أن يكون لغة وأن يكون إتباعا لحركة النون

ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r10.claim: An may be a masdariyya with an omitted preposition, or explanatory because the familiar sense of revelation implies speech; Abu Hayyan objects that inspiration has no speech, but the author says this overlooks that implication.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r10.anchor: و أن إما مصدرية بتقدير باء الملابسة أي بأن اتخذي أو تفسيرية وما بعدها مفسر للإيحاء

ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r11.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r11.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that explanatory an is unsuitable because revelation here unanimously means inspiration, which does not involve speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r11.anchor: وقد غفل عن ذلك أبو حيان أو لم يعتبره فقال : إن في ذلك نظرا لأن الوحي هنا بمعنى الإلهام إجماعا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r12.claim: The nests are called houses by metaphor: a human house is a dwelling, and the bees' nest resembles one in skilled construction and balanced division.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r12.anchor: وأصل البيت مأوى الإنسان واستعمل هنا في الوكر الذي تبنيه النحل لتعسل فيه تشبيها له بما يبنيه الإنسان

ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r13.claim: A reading pronounces buyutan with kasra on the first consonant to match the following ya; the usual plural of faʿl follows fuʿul with damma.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p181#2/r13.anchor: وقريء ( بيوتا ) بكسر الباء لمناسبة الياء وإلا فجمع فعل على فعول بالضم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd and others understand what people trellis as raised vines.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r1.anchor: أي يعرشه الناس أي يرفعه من الكروم كما روي عن ابن زيد وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r2.speaker: الطبري
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r2.claim: Al-Tabari is cited for interpreting the structures as roofs.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r2.anchor: أو السقوف كما نقل عن الطبري

ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r3.speaker: بعض
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r3.claim: Some take the structures more broadly to include both meanings.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r3.anchor: أو أعم منهما كما قال البعض

ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r4.claim: Min in the three phrases is partitive both by individual and by location: bees do not nest in every mountain, tree, trellis, or place within them.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r4.anchor: و ( من ) في المواضع الثلاثة للتبعيض بحسب الإفراد وبحسب الأجزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r5.claim: Some say min is partitive only by individuals; its locational sense must come from context because min cannot denote both senses at once.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r5.anchor: وبعضهم قال : إن ( من ) للتبعيض بحسب الإفراد فقط والمعنى الآخر معلوم من خارج لا من مدلول ( من )

ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r6.claim: Ibn Kamal wrote a separate treatise on the issue of min's partitive meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r6.anchor: ولمولانا ابن كمال تأليف مفرد في المسئلة فليراجع

ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r7.claim: The phrasing also employs antithesis alongside the coming description, and many commentators understand the houses as the structures bees build.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r7.anchor: وأياما كان ففيه مع ما يأتي قريبا إن شاء الله تعالى من البديع صنعة الطباق

ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r8.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r8.claim: Abu Hayyan takes the houses to be natural cavities in mountains and hollow trees, plus human-made hives and cavities in walls, so the command covers both wild and tended bees.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182/r8.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : الظاهر أنها عبارة عن الكوي التي تكون في الجبال وفي متجوف الأشجار والخلايا التي يصنعها ابن آدم للنحل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r1.claim: Revelation to bees means inspiration placed within them, which they understand; al-nahl here are honey wasps, singular nahla.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r1.anchor: أي: ألهمها وقذف في أنفسها، ففهمته، والنحل: زنابير العسل، واحدتها نحلة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r2.claim: People build places for bees among mountains, trees, and trellises, where the bees shelter.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r2.anchor: وقد جرت العادة أن أهلها يبنون لها الأماكن، فهي تأوي إليها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the trellises as vineyards.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r1.claim: God inspired the bees by instilling guidance and casting it into their hearts; a reading vowels النحل with fatḥatayn.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r1.anchor: ألهمها وقذف في قلوبها، وقرىء { إلى النحل } بفتحتين

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r2.claim: The أن after inspiration may stand for بأن, or introduce an explanation because inspiration carries the sense of speech; the feminine pronoun follows meaning although النحل is masculine.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون { أن } مفسرة لأن في الإيحاء معنى القول، وتأنيث الضمير على المعنى

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r3.claim: The partitive wording matters because bees do not build in every mountain, tree, trellis, or place within them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r3.anchor: ذكر بحرف التبعيض لأنها لا تبني في كل جبل وكل شجر

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r4.claim: Calling the bees' structure a house likens it to human construction: its fine workmanship and proportions exceed even skilled engineers without precise tools and thought; this may be mentioned to highlight that wonder.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r4.anchor: لما فيه من حسن الصنعة وصحة القسمة التي لا يقوى عليها أحذق المهندسين

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r5.claim: A reading has بيوتا with kasra on bāʾ, and Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read يعرشون with ḍamma on rāʾ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r5.anchor: وقرىء { بيوتا } بكسر الباء، وقرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر { يعرشون } بضم الراء

SULAMI:v1p368#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p368#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p368#3/r1.claim: God inspired the bee, directed it to its dwelling place, and taught it how to make what is in its belly and lay it only on clean stone or wood.
SULAMI:v1p368#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ألهمها ودلها على الموضع وعلمها . كيف تصنع ما في بطنها ولا تضعه إلا على حجر صاف

BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r1.claim: The bee's case is more striking and precious evidence of perfect power and wisdom than the preceding examples, so it concludes the triad; its later placement reflects its lower status in people's estimation, and 'revelation' signals its marvel.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r1.anchor: ولما كان أمر النحل في الدلالة على تمام القدرة وكمال الحكمة أعجب مما تقدم وأنفس , ثلث به وأخره

BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r2.claim: The phrase 'your Lord' recalls the beneficence that provides honey in remote wilderness and other places, demonstrating deliberate action and complete power.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r2.anchor: أي المحسن إليك بجعل العسل في مفاوز البراري المقفرة المفرطة المرارة وغيرها من الأماكن

BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r3.claim: God's revelation to the bee occurs by inspiration.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r3.anchor: إلى النحل } أي بالإلهام ؛ قال الرازي في اللوامع

BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r4.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r4.claim: Al-Razi says God gave each creature its form and then guided it: inanimate things by compulsion, bees, silk worms, and spiders by inspiration and compulsion, angels also by reason in a consistent order, and humans by all these plus thought and discernment.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r4.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : فالله تعالى أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r5.claim: Because revelation implies speech, أن introduces an explanation of what the bee is commanded to do.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r5.anchor: ولما كان في الإيحاء معنى القول , أتى ب ( أن ) المفسرة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r6.claim: The bee is commanded to make homes in mountains, suitable trees in groves, mountains, or deserts, and structures people raise such as roofs and walls.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r6.anchor: الصالحة لذلك في الغياض والجبال والصحارى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r7.claim: Homes are mentioned first because their craftsmanship, shape, construction, and proportion are astonishing.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p285/r7.anchor: وبدأ بالبيوت لأنها من عجب الدهر في حسن الصنعة وبداعة الشكل

DURR-FULL:v5p144/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p144/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p144/r1.claim: The account says people take their bees to pasture and travel with them as the bees follow; it also cites the image of livestock made subject to people.
DURR-FULL:v5p144/r1.anchor: فهم يخرجون بالنحل وينتجعون بها ويذهبون وهي تتبعهم

AKHFASH:v2p417/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p417/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p417/r1.claim: Hijazi Arabic treats النحل as feminine, while other Arabs use masculine هو النحل.
AKHFASH:v2p417/r1.anchor: وقال {إلى النحل أن اتخذي} على التأنيث في لغة اهل الحجاز. وغيرهم يقول "هو النحل"

AKHFASH:v2p417/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p417/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p417/r2.claim: The source generalizes that collectives whose singular differs only by ة are feminine in the cited dialect, as with البر and الشعير.
AKHFASH:v2p417/r2.anchor: كذلك كل جمع ليس بينه وبين واحده الا الهاء نحو "البر" و"الشعير" هو في لغتهم مؤنث.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p245#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p245#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p245#3/r1.claim: God's waḥy to the bee means either inspiring it or subjecting it; waḥy can occur through speech, indication, or subjection.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p245#3/r1.anchor: أي: ألهمها. وقيل:] سخرها. وقد بينت في كتاب "المشكل" أنه قد يكون كلاما وإشارة وتسخيرا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p245#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p245#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p245#3/r2.claim: Anything raised or trellised, such as a vine, plant, or roof, is an ʿarsh or maʿrūsh.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p245#3/r2.anchor: كل شيء عرش من كرم أو نبات أو سقف: فهو عرش ومعروش.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r1.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak reports from Ibn ʿAbbas that God’s revelation to the bee means inspiration; Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and Muqatil agree.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنه إلهام رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس وبه قال مجاهد والضحاك ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r2.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r2.claim: Al-ʿAwfi reports from Ibn ʿAbbas that the revelation means a command.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r2.anchor: والثاني أنه أمر رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r3.speaker: ابن مجاهد عن أبيه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r3.claim: Ibn Mujahid reports from his father that God sent the bee to its task.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r3.anchor: وروى ابن مجاهد عن أبيه قال أرسل إليها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r4.claim: The Arabic al-naḥl refers to honeybees, and one bee is called naḥla.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r5.claim: The verb yaʿrishun means to make a trellis; Ibn ʿAmir and Abu Bakr read it with a ḍamma on rāʾ, one of two dialectal forms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r5.anchor: ويعرشون يجعلونه عريشا وقرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم يعرشون بضم الراء وهما لغتان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies what people trellis as grapevines.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r6.anchor: أحدهما ما يعرشون من الكروم قاله ابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r7.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r7.claim: Al-Farraʾ identifies what people trellis as the roofs of houses.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r7.anchor: والثاني أنها سقوف البيوت قاله الفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba says any trellised vine, plant, or roof can be called an ʿarsh or maʿrush.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة كل شيء عرش من كرم أو نبات أو سقف فهو عرش ومعروش

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r9.speaker: قول
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r9.claim: A further view takes the trellised places as structures people build for bees to deposit honey; divine subjugation makes the bees shelter there.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p465#2/r9.anchor: وقيل المراد مما يعرشون مما يبنون لهم من الأماكن التي تلقي فيها تلقي فيها العسل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p581#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p581#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p581#3/r1.claim: The revelation to the bees means inspiration, guidance, and direction to make homes in mountains, trees, and human-built trellises.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p581#3/r1.anchor: المراد بالوحي هاهنا: الإلهام والهداية والإرشاد إلى النحل أن تتخذ من الجبال بيوتا تأوي إليها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p581#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p581#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p581#3/r2.claim: Bees construct their hexagonal combs with such precision and close packing that no gaps remain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p581#3/r2.anchor: ثم هي محكمة في غاية الإتقان في تسديسها ورصها، بحيث لا يكون بينها خلل.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r1.claim: Revelation to the bee is inspiration, inward prompting, and teaching in a manner whose mechanism no one can know.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r1.anchor: الإيحاء إلى النحل : إلهامها والقذف في قلوبها وتعليمها على وجه هو أعلم به ، لا سبيل لأحد إلى الوقوف عليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r2.claim: The bee's craft, delicate management, and accurate pursuit of its welfare plainly show that God gave it knowledge and discernment, as He gives reason to rational beings.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r2.anchor: دلائل بينة شاهدة على أن الله أودعها علما بذلك وفطنها ، كما أولى أولي العقول عقولهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r3.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r3.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb reads “the bee” with both initial vowels open; the noun is masculine, while feminine agreement follows its meaning.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r3.anchor: قرأ يحيى بن وثاب { إلى النحل } بفتحتين . وهو مذكر كالنحل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r4.claim: “That it take” is an explanatory particle because revelation here carries the sense of saying.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r4.anchor: هي أن المفسرة ؛ لأن الإيحاء فيه معنى القول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r5.claim: A reading pronounces the bāʾ in “houses” with kasra because of the following yāʾ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r5.anchor: وقرىء : ( بيوتا ) بكسر الباء لأجل الياء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r6.claim: The verb for raising structures is read with the rāʾ either kasra or ḍamma and means raising roofs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r6.anchor: و { يعرشون } بكسر الراء وضمها : يرفعون من سقوف البيوت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, the phrase can mean the places people make for bees in mountains, trees, and houses where honey forms; the pronoun refers to people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r7.anchor: وقيل : ما يبنون للنحل في الجبال والشجر والبيوت من الأماكن التي تتعسل فيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r8.claim: The preposition “from” means some of each kind: bees do not make homes in every mountain, tree, or built place.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p576#2/r8.anchor: أريد معنى البعضية ، وأن لا تبني بيوتها في كل جبل وكل شجر وكل ما يعرش

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r1.claim: God's revelation to the bee means inspiration.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r1.anchor: أحدها : أن الوحي إليها هو إلهاما , قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, it means that God subjected the bee to this behavior.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r2.anchor: الثاني : يعني أنه سخرها , حكاه ابن قتيبة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, God placed the behavior in the bee's instinct in a way hidden from other creatures.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r3.anchor: الثالث : أنه جعل ذلك في غرائزها بما يخفى مثله على غيرها , قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r4.claim: The bee's homes reflect the sound division and strong defense built into its inspired or instinctive nature.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r4.anchor: فذكر بيوتها لما ألهمها وأودعه في غرائزها من صحة القسمة وحسن المنعة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r5.claim: The structures humans build in the verse are vineyards.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r5.anchor: أحدهما : أنه الكرم , قاله ابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر الطبري
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, they are the buildings people construct.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p198#2/r6.anchor: الثاني : ما يبنون , قاله أبو جعفر الطبري .

NASAFI-FULL:v2p262#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p262#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p262#2/r1.claim: The imperative to bees is feminine because nahl is a feminine noun on the pattern of nakhl/nakhlah; an is explanatory since revelation here carries the sense of speech.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p262#2/r1.anchor: هي أن المفسرة لأن الايحاء فيه معنى القول قال الزجاج واحد النحل نحلة كنحل ونخلة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p262#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p262#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p262#2/r2.claim: The preposition min indicates some mountains, trees, or human-built structures, since bees do not build in every such place; yʿarishūn refers to people raising roofs or making hives.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p262#2/r2.anchor: يرفعون من سقوف البيت أو ما يبنون للنحل في الجبال والشجر والبيوت

NASAFI-FULL:v2p262#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p262#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p262#2/r3.claim: The pronoun in yʿarishūn refers to people.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p262#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p262#2/r4.speaker: شامي وأبو بكر
NASAFI-FULL:v2p262#2/r4.claim: Shāmī and Abū Bakr read the rāʾ of yʿarishūn with ḍamma.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r1.claim: Wahy can mean inspiration: God creates an awareness in the heart directly, without an apparent cause.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r1.anchor: قد يكون بمعنى الإلهام، وهو ما يخلقه الله تعالى في القلب ابتداء من غير سبب ظاهر

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r2.claim: Qurtubi cites the soul's inspiration toward wickedness and piety as an example of this meaning.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r3.claim: Animal instinct is another example: God gives animals awareness of benefits and harms and guides their livelihood.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك البهائم وما يخلق الله سبحانه فيها من درك منافعها واجتناب مضارها وتدبير معاشها.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r4.claim: The earth's telling its news is also attributed to God's inspiration of it.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r4.anchor: وقد أخبر عز وجل بذلك عن الموات فقال: { تحدث أخبارها } { بأن ربك أوحى لها }.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r5.speaker: إبراهيم الحربي
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r5.claim: Ibrahim al-Harbi says God has an unknown power over inanimate things; no messenger came to them, but God made them know by inspiration.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r5.anchor: قال إبراهيم الحربي: لله عز وجل في الموت قدرة لم يدر ما هي، لم يأتها رسول من عند الله ولكن الله تعالى عرفها ذلك أي ألهمها.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r6.claim: The interpreters agree that wahy in this verse means inspiration.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r6.anchor: ولا خلاف بين المتأولين أن الوحي هنا بمعنى الإلهام.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r7.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r7.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab reads ilā al-naḥl with the ḥāʾ vowel opened.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r7.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب «إلى النحل» بفتح الحاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r8.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives the bee's name from God's bestowal of the honey it produces.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r8.anchor: وسمي نحلا لأن الله عز وجل نحله العسل الذي يخرج منه قاله الزجاج.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r9.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r9.claim: Al-Jawhari says naḥl and naḥla mean a bee of either sex, also called yaʿsūb.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r9.anchor: والنحل والنحلة الدبر يقع على الذكر والأنثى، حتى يقال: يعسوب.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r10.claim: In Hijazi usage the collective noun naḥl is feminine; a collective may differ from its singular only by the feminine ending.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r10.anchor: والنحل يؤنث في لغة أهل الحجاز، وكل جمع ليس بينه وبين واحده إلا الهاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r11.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says all flies are in the Fire as punishment for its inhabitants except bees; al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim recorded it in Nawadir al-Usul.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r11.anchor:
وروي من حديث أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:
" الذبان كلها في النار يجعلها عذابا لأهل النار إلا النحل "
ذكره الترمذي الحكيم في نوادر الأصول.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet forbade killing ants, bees, hoopoes, and shrikes; Abu Dawud recorded it, and Qurtubi says it will recur in al-Naml.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r12.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس قال: نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قتل النملة والنحلة والهدهد والصرد، خرجه أبو داود أيضا، وسيأتي في «النمل» إن شاء الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r13.claim: Bees make homes in three settings: mountain cavities, hollow trees, and structures people prepare, including hives and walls.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r13.anchor: وإما فيما يعرش ابن آدم من الأجباح والخلايا والحيطان وغيرها.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r14.claim: The reference to mountain and tree homes applies when the bees have no owner.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r14.anchor: هذا إذا لم يكن لها مليك.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r15.claim: Here ʿarsh means to prepare; it often describes arranging branches and wood carefully to make shade.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r15.anchor: وعرش معناه هنا هيأ، وأكثر ما يستعمل فيما يكون من إتقان الأغصان والخشب وترتيب ظلالها

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r16.claim: The word is connected with the shelter built for the Prophet at Badr and with the term ʿarsh.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r16.anchor: ومنه العريش الذي صنع لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم بدر، ومن هذا لفظة العرش.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r17.claim: The verb ʿarasha is read with either kasra or ḍamma on the rāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r17.anchor: يقال: عرش يعرش ويعرش بكسر الراء وضمها، وقرىء بهما.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r18.speaker: ابن عامر
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAmir reads the verb with ḍamma; the other readers use kasra, while reports differ about ʿAsim.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r18.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر بالضم وسائرهم بالكسر، واختلف في ذلك عن عاصم.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r19.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r19.claim: Ibn al-Arabi marvels that bees are inspired to build hexagonal cells, which fit together seamlessly, whereas other polygons leave gaps.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:68/r19.anchor: قال ابن العربي: ومن عجيب ما خلق الله في النحل أن ألهمها لاتخاذ بيوتها مسدسة، فبذلك اتصلت حتى صارت كالقطعة الواحدة

RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r1.claim: The production of milk, sweet drink and good provision from dates and grapes (16:66–67), followed by honey from bees, proves a capable, freely acting, wise creator.
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r1.anchor: إخراج الألبان من النعم ، وإخراج السكر والرزق الحسن من ثمرات النخيل والأعناب دلائل قاهرة

RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r2.claim: Wahy here means inspiration: God established in bees' nature remarkable activities beyond the capacity of rational human beings.
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r2.anchor: يقال وحى وأوحى ، وهو الإلهام ، والمراد من الإلهام أنه تعالى قرر في أنفسها هذه الأعمال العجيبة

RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r3.claim: Bees build equal-sided hexagonal cells by instinct, while humans cannot make such cells without tools such as a ruler and compass.
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r3.anchor: أنها تبني البيوت المسدسة من أضلاع متساوية ، لا يزيد بعضها على بعض بمجرد طباعها

RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r4.claim: Geometry shows that other cell shapes necessarily leave wasted gaps, whereas hexagons fit without gaps; guiding a weak animal to this subtle wisdom is astonishing.
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r4.anchor: أنه ثبت في الهندسة أن تلك البيوت لو كانت مشكلة بأشكال سوى المسدسات فإنه يبقى بالضرورة فيما بين تلك البيوت فرج خالية ضائعة

RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r5.claim: The colony has a leader larger than the other bees who rules them; they serve and carry it while flying.
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r5.anchor: أن النحل يحصل فيما بينها واحد يكون كالرئيس للبقية ، وذلك الواحد يكون أعظم جثة من الباقي ، ويكون نافذ الحكم

RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r6.claim: When bees leave their hive as a group, people can bring them back by playing drums and musical instruments, whose melodies guide them home.
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r6.anchor: فإذا أرادوا عودها إلى وكرها ضربوا الطنبور والملاهي وآلات الموسيقى ، وبواسطة تلك الألحان يقدرون على ردها

RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r7.claim: Because these striking capacities are intelligence and judgment bestowed by inspiration, a state resembling revelation, God says He revealed to the bee.
RAZI-FULL:v20p56#2/r7.anchor: وكان حصول هذه الأنواع من الكياسة ليس إلا على سبيل الإلهام وهي حالة شبيهة بالوحي

RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r1.claim: Revelation to prophets is one distinct kind, illustrated by God's speaking to a human only by revelation in 42:51.
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r1.anchor: الوحي قد ورد في حق الأنبياء لقوله تعالى : { وما كان لبشر أن يكلمه الله إلا وحيا } ( الشورى : 51 )

RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r2.claim: Revelation also applies to saints, as in God's inspiration of the disciples in 5:111, and each kind has its own meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r2.anchor: وفي حق الأولياء أيضا قال تعالى : { وإذ أوحيت إلى } ( المائدة : 111 )

RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r3.claim: The word can mean inspiration to a human, as when God inspired Moses' mother in 28:7.
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r3.anchor: وبمعنى الإلهام في حق البشر قال تعالى : { يحذرون وأوحينا إلى أم موسى } ( القصص : 7 )

RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r4.claim: Revelation can also mean inspiration to other animals, as in the bee passage; each category has a distinct sense.
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r4.anchor: وفي حق سائر الحيوانات كما في قوله : { وأوحى ربك إلى النحل }

RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r5.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj suggests the bee is called naḥl because God bestowed the honey from its body on people.
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج : يجوز أن يقال سمي هذا الحيوان نحلا ، لأن الله تعالى نحل الناس العسل الذي يخرج من بطونها

RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r6.speaker: غيره
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r6.claim: Another linguist says naḥl is used as masculine or feminine, but is feminine in Hijazi speech, which explains the feminine form here; plurals ending in tāʾ are similarly feminine.
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r6.anchor: وقال غيره النحل يذكر ويؤنث ، وهي مؤنثة في لغة الحجاز ، ولذلك أنثها الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r7.claim: A plural whose singular differs only by the feminine tāʾ is treated as feminine.
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r7.anchor: وكذلك كل جمع ليس بينه وبين واحده إلا الهاء

RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r8.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r8.claim: The author of al-Kashshaf reads an as explanatory because revelation includes the sense of saying.
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r8.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : { أن اتخذى } هي ( أن ) المفسرة ، لأن الإيحاء فيه معنى القول

RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r9.claim: A reading has buyutan with kasra on the bāʾ.

RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r10.claim: The phrase about what people erect means what they build and roof; two readings differ in the vowel of rāʾ.
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r10.anchor: ومما يعرشون } أي يبنون ويسقفون ، وفيه لغتان قرىء بهما ، ضم الراء وكسرها

RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r11.claim: There are wild bees dwelling in mountains and woods without human care, and managed bees dwelling in people's hives; the verse's first phrases refer to the former and its last to the latter.
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r11.anchor: واعلم أن النحل نوعان : النوع الأول : ما يسكن في الجبال والغياض ولا يتعهدها أحد من الناس . والنوع الثاني : التي تسكن بيوت الناس

RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r12.claim: The preposition min expresses partiality: bees do not build in every mountain or tree, only in places suited to their needs.
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r12.anchor: أريد به معنى البعضية ، وأن لا تبني بيوتها في كل جبل وشجر ، بل في مساكن توافق مصالحها وتليق بها

RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r13.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r13.claim: Some hold that animals possess reason and can be addressed by God's commands and prohibitions.
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r13.anchor: فمن الناس من يقول لا يبعد أن يكون لهذه الحيوانات عقول ، ولا يبعد أن يتوجه عليها من الله تعالى أمر ونهي

RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r14.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r14.claim: Others deny that interpretation and say God created instincts and dispositions in animals that necessitate these behaviors.
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r14.anchor: وقال آخرون : ليس الأمر كذلك بل المراد منه أنه تعالى خلق فيها غرائز وطبائع توجب هذه الأحوال

RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r15.claim: Al-Razi points to his fuller discussion of the question under the story of the ant in 27:18.
RAZI-FULL:v20p57/r15.anchor: والكلام المستقصى في هذه المسألة مذكور في تفسير قوله تعالى : { نملة يأيها النمل ادخلوا مساكنكم } ( النمل : 18 )

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r1.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r1.claim: The bee's revelation can mean God inspiring it or placing in its heart knowledge unique to the creature.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r1.anchor: understood by some to refer to God’s inspiring the bee or placing a certain kind of knowledge in its heart that is unique to this creature

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r2.claim: Awḥā can denote formal scriptural revelation or other divine communication and inspiration, as in several other verses.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r2.anchor: Revealed translates awḥā, which is derived from a root often used in the Quran for Divine Revelation in a formal, scriptural sense

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r3.claim: The bee's revelation may metaphorically describe the instinctive behaviors God implanted in it.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r3.anchor: may simply be a metaphorical way of referring to the innate, instinctual behaviors that God has implanted in the bee

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r4.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī allows that bees may possess intelligence, shown by their intricate hexagonal hives and social organization under an obeyed leader.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r4.anchor: al-Rāzī suggests that it is at least possible that bees can be said to possess intelligence, including the ability to know God’s commands and prohibitions

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r5.claim: A literal reading fits descriptions of creatures as religious communities, praising God, and prostrating to Him.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r5.anchor: all creatures as constituting an ummah, that is, a religious community (6:38)

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r6.claim: The instruction concerns bees making hives in mountains, trees, and structures people build.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r6.anchor: construction of hives in the mountains and the trees as well as in that which they build

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r7.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r7.claim: That which people build can refer to human structures and their roofs.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r7.anchor: in the structures and roofs of human buildings (R, Ṭū, Z).

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r8.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r8.claim: The phrase may instead refer to beehives people construct to keep bees and obtain honey.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r8.anchor: may also refer to the beehives constructed by human beings for keeping bees and obtaining their honey (Q).

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r9.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r9.claim: Following the Lord's easy ways means following the process God taught the bee for making honey.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r9.anchor: follow the process God has taught it for making honey (Z)

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r10.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r10.claim: Alternatively, the bee is to follow paths to the fruits God ordained it to eat.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r10.anchor: follow the paths by which it may obtain the fruits that God has ordained for it to consume (R).

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r20.speaker: some Shiite commentators
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r20.claim: Some Shiite readings take the bee as ʿAlī and the Prophet's family, and its diverse drink as Quranic knowledge and wisdom in their teachings that heals spiritually.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r20.anchor: the bee here is a reference to ʿAlīand the family of the Prophet, and the drink of diverse hues refers symbolically to the knowledge of the Quran

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r21.speaker: al-Qurṭubī and al-Zamakhsharī
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r21.claim: Al-Qurṭubī and al-Zamakhsharī note this Shiite interpretation but reject its soundness.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r21.anchor: although its soundness is refuted by them

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r22.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r22.speaker: al-Ṭabrisī
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r22.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī traces the interpretation to ʿAlī saying he was the believers' yaʿsūb, a term meaning both male bee and leader or chieftain.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r22.anchor: al-Ṭabrisī indicates that this interpretation derives from ʿAlī’s statement that he was the yaʿsūb of the believers

SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r1.claim: أن اتخذي may be explanatory or infinitival; the objection to the explanatory reading is that inspiration contains no speech.
SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { أن اتخذي }: يجوز أن تكون مفسرة، وأن تكون مصدرية. واستشكل بعضهم كونها مفسرة.

SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r2.claim: He answers that objection: speech is appropriate to each thing according to its kind.
SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r2.anchor: وفيه نظر؛ لأن القول لكل شيء بحسبه.

SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r3.claim: Nahl is grammatically masculine or feminine as a generic noun; its feminine usage is the Hijazi dialect, reflected by اتخذي.
SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r3.anchor: والنحل: يذكر ويؤنث على قاعدة أسماء الأجناس. والتأنيث فيه لغة الحجاز، وعليها جاء { أن اتخذي }.

SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r4.speaker: ابن وثاب
SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r4.claim: His reading of النحل may reflect an independent dialect or vowel-following assimilation.
SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب " النحل " فيحتمل أن يكون لغة مستقلة، وأن يكون إتباعا.

SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r5.claim: من الجبال is partitive because bees cannot make homes in every mountain or tree; the discussion also refers back to readings of يعرشون in 7:137.
SAMIN-DURR:16:68/r5.anchor: و { من الجبال } " من " فيه للتبعيض؛ إذ لا يتهيأ لها ذلك في كل جبل ولا شجر.

TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r1.claim: God inspired the bees to build homes in mountains, trees, and human-built elevated structures or trellises.
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r1.anchor: الذي قلنا في ذلك قال أهل التأويل

TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r2.claim: God's revelation to the bees means that he inspired them.
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد: {وأوحى ربك إلى النحل} [النحل: 68] قال: «ألهمها إلهاما»

TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r3.speaker: معمر
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r3.claim: A report relayed by Maʿmar glosses the revelation as something cast into the bees' inner selves.
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r3.anchor: أخبرنا معمر، قال: بلغني في قوله: {وأوحى ربك إلى النحل} [النحل: 68] قال: «قذف في أنفسها»

TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r4.speaker: أصحاب معمر
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r4.claim: They describe the inspiration as instilling in the bees the instruction to make homes in mountains.

TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r5.claim: He says God commanded the bees to eat fruits and follow their Lord's paths gently.
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وأوحى ربك إلى النحل} [النحل: 68] الآية، قال: «أمرها أن تأكل من الثمرات

TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r6.claim: He notes that he explained the phrase about what people raise elsewhere and does not restate its meaning here.

TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r7.claim: He interprets what people raise as grapevines.
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {يعرشون} [النحل: 68] قال: «الكرم»

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r1.claim: Waḥā and awḥā are equivalent; here God's revelation to the bee is inspiration placed within it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وأوحى ربك} الآية. وحى وأوحى واحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r2.claim: The bee is the honey-making wasp, and its singular is naḥla.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj suggests the bee is named for being a gift from which God gives people honey.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: جائز أن يكون سمي نحلا؛ لأن الله عز وجل نحل الناس العسل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r4.claim: Another view says النحل can be masculine or feminine; it is feminine in Hijaz Arabic, as in the verse, and plurals marked only by a feminine ending are feminine.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r4.anchor: النحل يذكر ويؤنث (¬1)، وهي مؤنثة في لغة الحجاز

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r5.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r5.claim: God inspires every living creature to seek benefits and avoid harms; the bee is singled out as a striking lesson in subtle design, including its inspired construction of homes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r5.anchor: الله تعالى أوحى إلى كل دابة وذي روح وحي الإلهام في التماس منافعها واجتناب مضارها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r6.claim: Bees make homes for themselves in mountains when those places have no human owners.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p120#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هي تتخذ من الجبال لأنفسها إذا كانت لا أصحاب لها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p121/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p121/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p121/r1.claim: The phrase ومما يعرشون means what people build and roof; the verb was read with either a u-vowel or an i-vowel on the rāʾ, like two forms of يعكف.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p121/r1.anchor: أي: يبنون ويسقفون، وفيه لغتان: قرئ بها ضم الراء (¬4) وكسرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p121/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p121/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p121/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās understands it as hives that people build for bees.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p121/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد ما يعرش الناس لها من الجباح (¬6)؛ وهو: خلايا # النحل (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p121/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p121/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p121/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets what people trellis as grapevines, but the author rejects this here because bees do not inhabit vines; the intended construction is their hives.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p121/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد في قوله: {ومما يعرشون} هو الكروم (¬2)، ولا معنى للكروم هاهنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p121/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p121/r4.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p121/r4.claim: Without God's subjection and inspiration, bees would not live in the houses people build for them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p121/r4.anchor: لولا التسخير وإلهام الله تعالى ما كانت تأوي إلى ما يبني لها الناس من بيوتها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p267/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p267/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p267/r1.claim: وحي broadly means any conveyed indication: speech, writing, gesture, or a message; sending revelation to prophets is one instance, with Gabriel bringing the Quran.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p267/r1.anchor: كل شيء دللت به من كلام أو كتاب أو إشارة أو رسالة.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p267/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p267/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p267/r4.claim: وحي can mean inspiration: God inspired the disciples and the bees.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p267/r4.anchor: والوحي: إلهام، كقوله: وإذ أوحيت إلى الحواريين

ITQAN:v2p343/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p343/r20.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p343/r20.claim: God’s waḥy to the bees means that He inspired them.

ITQAN:v2p452#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p452#3/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v2p452#3/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls an explanatory here; the author rejects this because revelation to the bee is unanimously inspiration, not speech, so an is a verbal noun meaning “making.”
ITQAN:v2p452#3/r3.anchor: وزعم الزمخشري أن التي في قوله

DAMGHANI:v1p82/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p82/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p82/r4.claim: بيوت can mean nests or dwellings; the spider's woven home is an example.
DAMGHANI:v1p82/r4.anchor: الثامن : البيت بمعنى العش . قوله تعالى النحل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r13.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r13.claim: Bayt can mean a nest or hive, as in the bee and spider passages.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r13.anchor: والسابع : العش ، ومنه قوله تعالى في النحل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r7.claim: Wahy can mean inspiration, including inspiration of the disciples, bee, and Moses’ mother.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r7.anchor: والثالث : الإلهام . ومنه قوله تعالى في المائدة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p74/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p74/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p74/r1.claim: He allows that القول can be called revelation, as can gestures and lip or eyebrow signals; any sign that conveys meaning may be called revelation, while the bee's revelation is its being directed to build, follow paths, and eat fruit.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p74/r1.anchor: فما ننكر أن القول قد يسمى وحيا، والإيماء وحيا، والرمز بالشفتين والحاجبين وحيا، والإلهام وحيا
